description: Regression cases for the translation pipeline. Every case names an image in fixtures/ and the invariants that were broken before the fix, so the fix cannot silently come back. Run with: npm run regression

cases.note: A balloon that holds one character keeps one character. 円 became 日圓 and then 是錢.
A Japanese honorific becomes the Chinese one: 伯爵様 → 伯爵大人, at any effort, whatever type the reader gave.
うっ… / うつ… is a moan, not the noun 憂鬱. It was 憂鬱 at off and 鬱悶 at high. The reader writes it as うっ…, うつ…, うぅ… or even う….., so the case matches any う that is not うん.
The same moan at the other effort: both levels must agree. The reader writes it as うっ…, うつ…, うぅ… or even う….., so the case matches any う that is not うん.
The reader turns ねえ into お元 / 我元 / 我死. The block-level confirmation must hand kana to the translator, whatever the kana spelling of this run is.
この2人連れて勝手に動かせてもらうことにしたんだよ is one balloon and must stay one group, one sentence.
Every translated block is erased where the det plane says text; a stroke the plane missed still goes with the ink it runs into. Leftover ink ≤ 2% of a block's strokes.
A block whose columns were only partly labelled is still erased whole (可哀想な / エルマ…).

The blk head returned the name plate twice: a tight box and a loose one that also covered the 人生の負け組だ caption. Both rows were read, so one group's source held 未婚独身彼女ナシ平社員 twice and a second group repeated 花岡修太郎 / 三十九歳 as one joined line. The page then carried two labels on the same columns and the translation repeated (沒女友, 基層職員 / 普通職員, 人生失敗組).

A leaned block is still leaned, its columns are all read, and the labels follow the ink. The reader says direction v with lean 0 for the TV speech at 320,580, and the detector boxes its three columns as one rectangle. On the device the columns are found in the ink and read upright, and that reading goes into the block prompt as a reference, so the speech comes back as three lines instead of two. The labels must lean with the ink (about -16deg, counter-clockwise, not the +5 the run's diagonal measures) and the translation must carry 英雄. The banner's label must be ~60px, the tight column in its 169x358 leaned box, not the 96-160 the axis aligned box gives; the tolerance is wider on that side because a nine character translation is fitted down to 0.6 of it.

groups.source: やっ|やつ|ヒーロ|熱いな

cases.note: The glyph size is measured from the page, not read off the grid by the model. On this page the reader answered em 44 and then em 13 for the same 27 pixel column in two runs, and a 13 pixel answer drew the label at a third of the source. Each label must be within +-30% of its own column: 27px for the cup speech, 30px for 2カ月後の試験で, 42px for 訓練校を退学してもらいます. The reader's em must not decide any of them.

The two columns in the shield bubble (二人はその隙に / 魔法で攻撃してくれ) were drawn on a detector box that starts above the glyphs, so the translation sat outside the bubble. On the full page that block is BLK 483,1168 66×256; this export is 720×1024, so the same rectangle is 309,748 42×164. The drawn characters of both columns stay inside that rectangle.

The note in the coffin (BLK 553,365 241x197) is three rows of horizontal text on a sheet tilted about -32 degrees (counter-clockwise). The det head fits one leaned box to the ink (265x31), so the reader's three entries all name that one blue rectangle. The layout used to band-split the box's page rectangle (241x165, most of it rotation), give each row 55px, draw all three at the same 267px glyph in the same place, and stack them over the artwork. Three lines, parallel, at the sheet's lean, each about the source glyph size, none on another.
